description:
Wire PKIX-6vu (input guards), PKIX-yqb (trust anchor), PKIX-vxf (walk loop),
and PKIX-gry (validity/ext/CA/pathLen) into the single public validate_path() function.

## What

validate_path<V>(chain, anchors, policy, verifier) -> Result<ValidatedPath>:
  1. check_inputs(chain, anchors)?                     // PKIX-6vu
  2. check_oid_consistency(chain)?                     // PKIX-6vu
  3. let anchor_index = find_trust_anchor(...)?        // PKIX-yqb
  4. initialize working_issuer_name, working_spki      
  5. for i in (0..chain.len()).rev():                  // PKIX-vxf + PKIX-gry
       verify_signature(...)?, names_match(...)?,
       check_validity(...)?, check_critical_extensions(...)?,
       [if intermediate: CA/pathLen/KeyUsage checks]
  6. return Ok(ValidatedPath { anchor_index, depth: chain.len() - 1 })

## Documentation fix
Add to ValidationPolicy::current_time_unix rustdoc:
  '/// Warning: passing u64::MAX causes all notAfter checks to pass — treat as permissive mode.'

## Tests
- Happy-path 1-cert chain (self-signed leaf as anchor) -> Ok(ValidatedPath { anchor_index: 0, depth: 0 })
- Happy-path 3-cert chain (leaf + intermediate + root) -> Ok(ValidatedPath { anchor_index: 0, depth: 2 })
- Verify anchor_index is correct when anchors slice has multiple entries
- Verify depth is chain.len() - 1

## Depends on
PKIX-6vu, PKIX-yqb, PKIX-vxf, PKIX-gry
notes:
SECURITY REQUIREMENTS (from security surface analysis — all must be implemented in this bead):

1. EMPTY CHAIN GUARD: validate_path must check chain.is_empty() as its FIRST action. Return Err(Error::NoTrustedPath) or add a new EmptyChain variant. A bare loop over 0..chain.len()-1 panics on empty chain in debug mode (usize underflow).

2. ALGORITHM OUTER/INNER CONSISTENCY: RFC 5280 §4.1.1.2 requires cert.signature_algorithm (outer) == cert.tbs_certificate.signature (inner). This check belongs in validate_path, not only in pkix-chain-simple. Check for every cert in the chain before calling the SignatureVerifier. Return Err(Error::SignatureInvalid { index }) on mismatch. Oracle: openssl verify rejects these certs.

3. TRUST ANCHOR MATCHING MUST COMPARE SPKI, NOT ONLY NAME: find_trust_anchor must compare both subject name AND SubjectPublicKeyInfo against TrustAnchor fields. Name-only matching allows a self-signed leaf with the same subject name as a real anchor to spoof the trust anchor. After PKIX-o76, TrustAnchor holds subject + SPKI directly.

4. CRITICAL NAMECONSTRAINTS MUST BE REJECTED IN V0.1: v0.1 scope is 'no NameConstraints enforcement' — but if a cert carries a CRITICAL NameConstraints extension (OID 2.5.29.30), it MUST be rejected via Error::UnhandledCriticalExtension. Silently ignoring a critical NameConstraints extension is a security vulnerability. The critical-extension guard (PKIX-ad6) must include NameConstraints in its 'reject if critical' list.

5. PER-CERT pathLenConstraint ENFORCEMENT: state machine must track max_path_length dynamically per RFC 5280 §6.1.4(l)(m). It is NOT sufficient to compare chain.len() against policy.max_path_len only. When a cert has pathLenConstraint present and less than current max_path_length, update max_path_length. Use checked/saturating arithmetic — never bare u8 decrement. A pathLenConstraint of 4294967295 (u32::MAX from x509-cert) must be handled without overflow when stored/compared as u8.

6. u64::MAX TIME IS PERMISSIVE: now_unix = u64::MAX passes all notAfter checks. Add a note to the validity period check that this is a caller footgun; the implementation itself is correct (it follows the spec), but the docstring of ValidationPolicy::current_time_unix must warn about this.
